title: When, on Devotion's Seraph Wing
description: When, on Devotion's Seraph Wing in Tonic Solfa to ALL SAINTS, NEW, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Sarah Elizabeth Miles wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 359, “Foretaste of Heaven”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ALL SAINTS, NEW; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: When, on de-vo-tion's ser-aph wing, The spir-it soars a-bove, And feels Thy pre-sence, Fa-ther, Friend, God of e-ter-nal love! The joys of earth, how swift they fade Be-fore that liv-ing ray, Which gives to the rapt soul a glimpse Of pure and per-fect day!

lines: And feels Thy presence, Father, Friend,
The joys of earth, how swift they fade
Which gives to the rapt soul a glimpse
A gleam of Heaven's own light, though now
Through the pale shadows that are spread
But Thine unclouded smile, O God!
Where we shall know as we are known,
And see Thee, face to face.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Sarah Elizabeth Miles died in 1877.
credits: Words by Sarah Elizabeth Miles (1807–1877), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ALL SAINTS, NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
